You are diagnosing a reported bug. If a reference (log, stack trace, repro steps) is attached, read it and reproduce the failure before writing a fix — do not guess at root cause from the description alone. If nothing is attached, reproduce it yourself first.

Goal: Chat-UI Panel

We need to focus on UI improvments for the Chat UI which showns when a user makes selection. 

First few issues
(1) There is a horizontal scroll, The rendering of communication should avoid horitontal scrolsl from existing 
(2) we need a bit sharper separation between the sub-componets within the chat so we can make more targeter imprvometns

Reference: /home/bilko/Projects/session-manager/session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/attachments/kc0s2uawa7-image.png

All green. Summary of the fixes:

**(1) Horizontal scroll** — root cause: `.prose-chat`/`.markdown-body` had no `overflow-wrap`, so a long unbroken token inside inline `code` (a commit subject, file path, session id) couldn't soft-wrap and pushed the chat column wider than its track. `overflow-y-auto` on the container then computes `overflow-x: auto` per spec, producing the scrollbar you saw. Fixed by:
- `styles.css`: added `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to `.markdown-body`/`.prose-chat`, `word-break: break-word` on their `code`.
- `ChatTranscriptTurn.tsx`: added `break-words` to the plain-text user bubble (not covered by `.prose-chat`).
- `EpicDetail.tsx`: added `break-words` to the response-event caption, `min-w-0` on the grid/turn wrappers (grid tracks default to content-based min-width and can overflow otherwise), and `overflow-x-hidden` on the scroll container as a hard backstop.

**(2) Sharper sub-component separation** in `EpicDetail.tsx`/`EpicComposer.tsx`: added `border-t`/`border-b` dividers between the title block, meta-stats row, and view-tabs row in the header; between the attached-PRDs bar and the timeline; and between the composer's "iterating in" context bar and its action toggle/input area — so each piece is now a distinct visually-bounded band instead of just spacing.

Typecheck, the selector lint, and all 72 epics unit tests pass.
